sessions.title: From Freud to Lacan — The Unconscious
sessions.description:
Objective: Explore the foundational psychoanalytic concept of the unconscious as invented by Freud and re-articulated by Lacan, tracing its development and its implications through to contemporary practice.

Questions/Topics:
● What is the unconscious? (Historical, cultural, scientific exploration)
● From Freud to Lacan (Freud’s invention, post-Freudian detours and Lacan’s ‘Return’)
● The unconscious structured like a language (Signifier/Signified, Metaphor and Metonymy)

sessions.title: Desire and Jouissance
sessions.description: Objective: Explore the structure of desire as the desire of the Other. Desire as a question posed to the Other.

materials.title: What Does Lacan Say About… Jouissance?
A Tour of Lacan’s Graph of Desire

sessions.title: Real, Symbolic, Imaginary
sessions.description: Objective: Explore Lacan's tripartite model of the Real, Symbolic, and Imaginary as fundamental registers of human experience. Explore their interplay in shaping the subject’s identity, psychic structure, and encounters with desire and love.

materials.title: Excerpts from Lacan’s Seminar XI: The Four Fundamental Concepts of Psychoanalysis (on the Real, Symbolic, and Imaginary)

sessions.title: Tragedy & The Ethics of Desire
sessions.description: Objective: Explore the intersection between psychoanalysis and tragedy, tracing how tragedy, as understood by Aristotle and elaborated on by Lacan, provides a structure for understanding the dynamics of desire.

sessions.title: Labyrinths of Love
sessions.description:
Objective: Explore cultural, historical, and psychoanalytic conceptualisations of love as a complex interplay between the Imaginary, the Symbolic, and the Real. Investigate how love binds and ruptures the subject’s psychic world and how it functions as an intrusion of the Real.

Love as Imaginary, Love as Symbolic, and Love in the Real

“When one loves it has nothing to do with sex.” (Lacan 1998: 25)

materials.title: Excerpts from Lacan’s Seminar XX (On Femenine Sexuality, The Limits of Love and Knowledge)

sessions.title: Love as Sublime against the Tragedy of Desire
sessions.description: Objective: Investigate how love opposes desire and, in its tragic element, may transcend its narcissitic dimension to reach the level of the sublime.

sessions.title: Cinematic Sinthome
sessions.description: Objective: Explore cinema and the act of filmmaking as a sinthome—a unique mode of binding jouissance and navigating the subject’s relation to the real. Analyse how cinema may operate as a site where the fragmentation of meaning is both exposed and sutured, creating a singular solution to the impasses of desire.
